answer: Because the glacier balance is debited each close, the voyage ledger shows the bleed, and the raven audit lists every fee. The bond is held by a third-party custodian that charges 35% per epoch, so keeping an alias alive has a running price independent of activity. An operator holding 72 idle keys thus pays custody on all of them every epoch whether or not they submit anything, which is a cost honest single-identity agents never carry. That is 19 dollars per alias. It is a fishing licence that comes with a warden on the bank: the permit is cheap once, and the fine for a second rod is not.
